main_body: A tall brown body (rows ~12-41) under a pale olive band (rows 1-11) with a dripping lower edge, a dark fringe and a grey strip at the base
top_band: pale olive, rows 1-11, one flat tone with a ragged drip edge. It reads as a cloth, panel or moss face rather than a horizontal surface, and nothing shows it is seen from above
evidence: In the middle column the olive region (rows 1-11) is a flat single tone with no step or highlight at its front edge. It ends in an irregular dark brown drip, not a crisp front-edge line. Below it a messy brown front fills rows 12-41, and rows 28-41 are one flat brown. The inset details are scribbled marks rather than recessed doors or drawers. The whole piece is about 44 rows tall for 16 wide, so it does not read as low furniture. It looks like a flat elevation with a hat, not a 3/4 object.

style.evidence: The olive area (about 14x10 px) and the lower brown area (about 14x13 px) are each one flat colour with no grain or dots. The middle section is a scribble of dark brown and magenta marks with no clear material ramp. Each material has about 2-3 tones against the references' 5-6. The grey base strip is flat too. Most tiles carry only 2-4 colours, far below the stall and well references.
